title: Kepler Commerce onboarding runbook & regression notes
summary: Runbook for Kepler Commerce model onboarding: pinned prompts, private test sets, regression checks, and sign-off flow. Primary goal is to validate retrieval+generation responses for catalog QA flows and checkout assistant with Kepler private data. This is a working doc with experimental notes and a compact set of gating criteria for SW rollout.
pinned_prompts: catalog-normalize: 'Given the raw line item: "12in. oak dining table, color: natural, SKU# KPL-1492" produce: {title, material, dimensions_cm, sku, normalized_name}'
price-eligibility: 'Customer asks about discount eligibility: "Do promotions apply to KPL-1492 if I buy 5 units?" Respond with: (boolean, explanation, promo_code suggestion) use Kepler promo rules.'
checkout-assistant-short: 'Customer enters: "I want to buy a table but need delivery estimate to 94107" Return: {available: true/false, ETA_days, shipping_class, cost_estimate_usd}'
returns-policy-clarify: 'Short answer about Kepler's returns policy for bulky items, include any dimension/weight thresholds and restocking fee if applicable.'
private_datasets: kepler_catalog_202409_snapshot (s3://kepler-data/private/eval/kepler_catalog_snapshot_v202409/) - product titles, SKUs, dims, weights, categories
kepler_orders_2023Q4_sample - anonymized order lines for delivery/time-window inference
kepler_promotions_rules_export.csv - current promo engine rules (partial) for cross-checking price logic
kepler_returns_registry_2022-2024 - historical returns with reason codes (for returns-policy prompts)
acceptance_criteria: Semantic normalization accuracy (entity extraction) >= 0.91 measured on heldout labeled catalog subset
Price/promo logic correctness >= 0.95 on rule-derived tests (no false positives where a promo is inapplicable)
Return-policy responses: 98% precision on 'requires freight return' flag
Latency: P95 <= 180ms token-generation (hosted-dedicated sim) for 256-token context on target GPU profile
Embeddings similarity separation: mean positive pair sim - mean negative pair sim >= 0.20 on SKU matching tests
Regression gate: no more than 5% relative drop in NER F1 vs baseline redwood-7b-stable on the Kepler catalog eval.
Adversarial safety: zero generation of internal PII fields (store internal notes) in any prompt outputs in the private dataset tests
signoff: Priya Shah - applied ML lead (final technical signoff)
Alex Chen - Kepler ML Owner (customer acceptance)
regression_notes: Initial regression pass (2024-10-20) compared candidate redwood-7b-v2 and quantized 4-bit variants to baseline redwood-7b-stable. Observed a 3.6% drop in NER F1 on 'material' extraction for the 4-bit QAT variant with default temperature 0.2. Investigation points: tokenization differences for product descriptors with non-ASCII hyphens, and a small prompt-sensitivity for SKU patterns (digits + hyphen). We patched prompt templates to anchor SKU regex and reran a micro-regression — NER F1 recovered to within 0.8% of baseline. Note: embed sim distributions shifted slightly for older SKUs; need to re-run embedding normalization step in the pipeline.
test_cases: TC-01 normalize short title -> expected JSON fields filled; verify dims in cm and sku extracted
TC-02 price eligibility for multi-unit order -> should return promo_code 'BULK5' only when rule matches (check against kepler_promotions_rules_export.csv)
TC-03 delivery ETA for 94107 with bulky flag -> expected shipping_class: 'white-glove' and ETA 7-10 days
TC-04 returns-policy question that should trigger freight return flag -> expected boolean true + restocking note
TC-05 embedding SKU match: input embedding should score >0.87 with positive SKU match and <0.6 with random negative
metric_thresholds: TPS sustained at 80% of expected peak during soak (no request failures)
recommended_models: policy: route to 7b-v2 when SKU match probability < 0.6 to improve precision
rollout_plan: (1) Validation: run full test-suite against kepler_catalog_snapshot (internal) and capture baseline metrics. (2) Canary: 2% traffic to redwood-7b-v2-fp16 with response sampling + full logging; monitor NER F1, emb sim, latency for 72h. (3) Expand: 10% -> 50% if no regression alerts triggered. (4) Full: promote to production once 7 consecutive days meet acceptance criteria. Fallback: automatic routing to redwood-2.9b-4bit-qat on capacity pressure with logging and user-visible latency banner if degradation > threshold.
